hook: This is a very short, lighthearted file about a rabbit the staff call "Walter". There is no twist to brace for; the pleasure is in how calmly the report lists the ridiculous things this small animal can do. It takes a couple of minutes to read and works well as a palate cleanser.
whyItMatters: SCP-524 is a good example of the cozy, almost cartoonish Safe-class object that sits alongside the wiki's horror. Its whole premise fits in one line, an ordinary pet with an appetite that ignores physics, and the report never strains to make it menacing. Entries like this show that the clinical format can carry gentle comedy just as well as dread.
thingsToNotice:
Notice the gap between the threat level and the paperwork. The procedures exist mostly to protect the site's equipment from the rabbit, and the line saying it needs no particular diet is a dry joke, since it can digest steel, glass and kilos of radioactive material without harm.

The centerpiece is Walter eating himself: he starts at the tail, works forward past his legs, then turns his mouth inside out to swallow his own head and vanishes, only to pop back up intact about half an hour later near the same spot. It is told in the same flat tone as the rest, which is what makes it funny. The addendum then reveals, almost in passing, that he was found during a major August blackout after chewing through several reactors at a power plant, still nibbling on a cable.
